info.title: SympleHost Partner API
info.description:
The **Partner API** lets an approved third-party PMS run alongside SympleHost — pull
reservations, transactions and unified-inbox messages, and link properties.

## Authentication
Per-account, scoped API keys. Two modes:

- **HTTP Basic** — only for a key whose scopes are **all** non-sensitive (read-only).
  `Authorization: Basic base64(key_id:secret)`.
- **HMAC-SHA256** — **mandatory on every request, GETs included,** for any key holding a
  *sensitive* scope (`guest_name:read`, `guest_contact:read`, `message_content:read`,
  `transactions:read`, `customers:read`, `reservations:write`, `pricing:write`,
  `availability:write`, `properties:link`, `messaging:send`, `webhooks:manage`, `reviews:write`).
  The check is per key, not per endpoint: `availability:read`, `pricing:read` and
  `reviews:read` are non-sensitive, but a key that also holds any sensitive scope gets
  `401 signature_required` on Basic even for those reads.
  Sign with the key's `signing_secret`:

  ```
  X-SH-Signature = hex( HMAC-SHA256( signing_secret,
    "<METHOD>\n<fullpath>\n<unix_ts>\n<sha256_hex(raw_body)>" ) )
  ```

  `<fullpath>` is the request path **including the query string**, exactly as sent
  (e.g. `/api/v1/partner/reservations?status=confirmed`).
  Send `X-SH-Key-Id`, `X-SH-Timestamp`, `X-SH-Signature`, plus a fresh `X-SH-Nonce` (UUID)
  on writes **and on every `webhooks:manage` call, GETs included**. Sending a nonce on
  every request is always safe. The timestamp window is **120s**. Empty body signs `sha256("")`.

## Conventions
- **Media type:** request `Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json`.
- **Pagination:** opaque keyset cursor — seed with `updated_since`, then follow `meta.next_cursor`.
  Feed is at-least-once; dedupe by `id`.
- **PII gating:** fields you lack scope for return `"***"`, listed in `meta.masked_fields` / `masked_fields`.
- **Errors:** single JSON:API `errors` envelope with stable machine `code`s — always
  `application/vnd.api+json`, even on endpoints whose success response is `application/json`.
- **Versioning:** `meta.payload_version` echoed on every response.

get.description:
Returns reservations for the account, newest-updated first, keyset-paginated.
Base fields need `reservations:read`; the financial summary needs `transactions:read`
and guest PII needs `guest_name:read` / `guest_contact:read` (all sensitive → HMAC).

x-codeSamples.label: Basic (read-only)
x-codeSamples.source:
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai/api/v1/partner/reservations?status=confirmed" \
  -u "$SH_KEY_ID:$SH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

x-codeSamples.label: HMAC (with PII/financials)
x-codeSamples.source:
# sensitive scopes ⇒ HMAC. Sign METHOD\npath\nts\nsha256(body); GET body is empty.
# The signed path INCLUDES the query string, byte-for-byte as sent.
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/reservations?status=confirmed"
HASH=$(printf %s "" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' GET "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

import time, hmac, hashlib, requests
BASE = "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai"
# Sign the path INCLUDING its query string, exactly as requested.
method, path = "GET", "/api/v1/partner/reservations?status=confirmed"
body = ""
ts = str(int(time.time()))
h = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
canon = f"{method}\n{path}\n{ts}\n{h}"
sig = hmac.new(SIGNING_SECRET.encode(), canon.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
res = requests.get(f"{BASE}{path}", headers={
    "X-SH-Key-Id": KEY_ID, "X-SH-Timestamp": ts, "X-SH-Signature": sig,
    "Accept": "application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json",
})
data = res.json()

post.summary: Create a reservation (push a direct booking)
post.description:
Pushes a partner-originated direct booking
into SympleHost as a `Reservation`. Requires `reservations:write` (sensitive → **HMAC**)
and an `Idempotency-Key` — a retried create must never double-book.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/reservations"
BODY='{"listing_id":"<uuid>","start_date":"2026-07-02","end_date":"2026-07-05","adults":2,"kids":1,"currency":"INR","total_amount":4500.0,"external_ref":"PMS-7781","guest":{"name":"Ada Lovelace","email":"ada@example.com","phone":"+15551234567"}}'
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

import time, json, hmac, hashlib, uuid, requests
BASE = "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai"
path = "/api/v1/partner/reservations"
body = json.dumps({
    "listing_id": "<uuid>", "start_date": "2026-07-02", "end_date": "2026-07-05",
    "adults": 2, "kids": 1, "currency": "INR", "total_amount": 4500.0, "external_ref": "PMS-7781",
    "guest": {"name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com", "phone": "+15551234567"},
})
ts = str(int(time.time()))
h = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
canon = f"POST\n{path}\n{ts}\n{h}"
sig = hmac.new(SIGNING_SECRET.encode(), canon.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
requests.post(f"{BASE}{path}", data=body, headers={
    "X-SH-Key-Id": KEY_ID, "X-SH-Timestamp": ts,
    "X-SH-Nonce": str(uuid.uuid4()), "X-SH-Signature": sig,
    "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4()), "Content-Type": "application/json",
})

post.description:
Changes the stay dates, guest count and/or total on a partner reservation.
Partner reservations are **external** — SH persists the supplied `total_amount`
verbatim and does **not** re-price from listing pricing or trigger a payment/refund
flow. Any linked bookings have their dates/guests updated so the stay reflects
natively. Requires `reservations:write` (sensitive → **HMAC**) and an `Idempotency-Key`.
A `cancelled`/`completed` reservation cannot be modified (422).

schema.description: Only the fields you send are changed.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/reservations/$RES_ID/modify"
BODY='{"start_date":"2026-07-11","end_date":"2026-07-15","guest_count":4,"total_amount":28000.0}'
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

`ReservationItem` is cancelled). Requires `reservations:write` (sensitive → **HMAC**)
and an `Idempotency-Key`. **Idempotent** — replaying on an already-cancelled
reservation returns `200` with the cancelled record.

get.description:
OTA guest reviews for the account's listings. `reviews:read`
(non-sensitive → Basic OK). Batched via keyset cursor. All filters are
optional; the default returns every review. `platform` narrows to a single
OTA; `start_date`/`end_date` bound `reviewed_at` (both inclusive). Default
order is newest-first (`sort=-created_at`); pass `sort` to change it.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Filter to a single OTA platform. Default = all platforms.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on `reviewed_at`. Default = no lower bound.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on `reviewed_at`. Default = no upper bound.

attributes.review_text: A lovely stay, spotless and well located.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai/api/v1/partner/reviews?platform=airbnb&start_date=2026-06-01" \
  -u "$SH_KEY_ID:$SH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

get.description:
One OTA guest review by id. `reviews:read` (non-sensitive → Basic OK).
Scoped to the account's listings — a review on another account's listing
returns `404`.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai/api/v1/partner/reviews/$REVIEW_ID" \
  -u "$SH_KEY_ID:$SH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

post.description:
Posts a host response to an OTA guest review. Requires `reviews:write`
(sensitive → **HMAC**) and a **mandatory** `Idempotency-Key` — a retried
respond must not double-post to the OTA. Attributed to the account's
partner system user.

**`meta.delivery` says whether the guest will ever see the reply. Read it.**

- `"sent"` — submitted to the OTA. The guest can see it.
- `"recorded"` — **stored on SympleHost only. It was NOT sent to the OTA and
  the guest will never see it.** A `200` here means the write succeeded, not
  that the reply was delivered.
- `"failed"` — the OTA rejected it. Returned as `422` with error code
  `channel_rejected` (never a `500`); nothing is stored.

The `reply_status` attribute on the returned review tells the two
`"recorded"` cases apart: `not_deliverable` means the review is OTA-linked
but its reply window has closed, so the reply is held locally and is
undeliverable; `null` means the review was never OTA-linked to begin with
(a direct or imported review), so local IS its only home.

A review that already has a `host_response` is never re-posted to the OTA,
whatever `can_reply` says — so an edit, or a retry with a fresh
`Idempotency-Key`, cannot put a second reply in front of the guest.

Whether that edit is accepted depends on where the stored reply lives:

- The reply is **already published on the channel** (`reply_status:
  "published"`, or `ota_is_replied: true`) → **`409`** with error code
  `reply_already_published`, and nothing is written. There is no way to change
  a posted reply from this API, so accepting the edit would leave your text
  here while the guest keeps reading the original. Edit it on the channel.
- The reply was only **recorded locally** (`reply_status: "not_deliverable"`,
  or `null` for a non-OTA review) → edited in place, `200` + `"recorded"`.

The same holds when the OTA reports a host reply whose text was never synced
here (`host_response` is null but the channel already shows one): the reply is
stored locally with `reply_status: "not_deliverable"` and returns
`"recorded"`, rather than being posted as a second guest-visible reply.

200.description: Response stored. Submitted to the OTA only when meta.delivery is "sent" — "recorded" means it was stored locally and NOT sent to the OTA.

attributes.review_text: A lovely stay, spotless and well located.
attributes.host_response: Thank you so much for the kind words!

409.description: The stored reply is already published on the channel and cannot be changed from here. Nothing was written.

errors.title: Reply already published
errors.detail: This reply is already published on the channel; edit it on the channel.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/reviews/$REVIEW_ID/respond"
BODY='{"data":{"attributes":{"response":"Thank you so much for the kind words!"}}}'
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

get.description:
The account's customers. Requires `customers:read` (sensitive → **HMAC required**).
Batched via keyset cursor. `search` is an optional case-insensitive match on
name, email, or phone (default = all). Guest PII is additionally gated:
`name` on `guest_name:read`, `email`/`phone` on `guest_contact:read`; withheld
fields return `"***"` and are listed in `masked_fields`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive match on name, email, or phone. Default = all.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/customers?search=ada"
HASH=$(printf %s "" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' GET "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

post.summary: Link a property to your external reference
post.description:
Store your PMS's external reference against an SH listing. Naturally idempotent —
requires `properties:link` (sensitive → **HMAC**). An `Idempotency-Key` is
**accepted but optional** here (dedup-only); unlike other writes it is not
enforced, because re-linking the same reference is a safe no-op.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional for linking (dedup-only) — the shared write-idempotency requirement is relaxed for this naturally-idempotent operation.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/properties/$LISTING_ID/link"
BODY='{"external_ref":"PMS-1001"}'
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

delete.description: Removes the block and restores availability. Needs `availability:write` (HMAC).

get.description:
One entry per inclusive date in `start_date`..`end_date` (max 370 days). Dates with no
override return the listing's default availability and no restrictions. Needs `availability:read`.

post.description:
Sets inventory and/or restrictions across one or more inclusive date ranges. Only the
fields you send are changed (others, including price, are preserved). Max 370 days per
entry and 500 dates total. Needs `availability:write` (sensitive → HMAC) and an `Idempotency-Key`.

get.description:
The listing's base-rate pricing rules — price bounds, extra-guest pricing, and
weekly/monthly + length-of-stay discounts. Complements the per-date pricing calendar.
Needs `pricing:read`. 404 if the listing has no base-rate season.

post.description:
Partial update of the base-rate pricing rules — send only the fields you want to change.
Needs `pricing:write` (sensitive → HMAC) and an `Idempotency-Key`. 404 if no base-rate season.

200.description: Updated settings (echoes the full current settings).

get.description:
One entry per inclusive date in `start_date`..`end_date` (max 370 days). `rate` is the
effective nightly rate (your `custom_rate` override wins; otherwise the season base, or
`null` if unset). Needs `pricing:read`.

post.summary: Bulk-set nightly rates and/or price bounds
post.description:
Sets the nightly `rate` across one or more inclusive date ranges (your per-date override),
and/or the listing's `min_price`/`max_price` bounds. Max 370 days per entry and 500 dates
total. Needs `pricing:write` (sensitive → HMAC) and an `Idempotency-Key`.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/properties/$PROPERTY_ID/pricing"
BODY='{"updates":[{"start_date":"2026-08-01","end_date":"2026-08-31","rate":199.5}],"min_price":120,"max_price":400}'
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

import time, json, hmac, hashlib, uuid, requests
BASE = "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai"
path = f"/api/v1/partner/properties/{PROPERTY_ID}/pricing"
body = json.dumps({"updates": [{"start_date": "2026-08-01", "end_date": "2026-08-31",
    "rate": 199.5}], "min_price": 120, "max_price": 400})
ts = str(int(time.time()))
h = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
canon = f"POST\n{path}\n{ts}\n{h}"
sig = hmac.new(SIGNING_SECRET.encode(), canon.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
requests.post(f"{BASE}{path}", data=body, headers={
    "X-SH-Key-Id": KEY_ID, "X-SH-Timestamp": ts,
    "X-SH-Nonce": str(uuid.uuid4()), "X-SH-Signature": sig,
    "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4()), "Content-Type": "application/json",
})

get.description: Unified-inbox threads. `messaging:read`. Guest fields gate on `guest_name:read`/`guest_contact:read`. Defaults to newest-created first (`sort=-created_at`); pass `sort` to change order.

parameters.name: listing_id
parameters.description: Only conversations linked to this property, by any of the three links the `property` attribute resolves (discussed listing, reservation's booking, or OTA-mapped listing). Note this is a superset of "threads whose `property.id` equals this value": a thread linked to two properties by different paths matches both, while `property` reports only the winning one. Must be a UUID; anything else returns `422 validation_failed`.

put.description:
Marks the conversation's inbound (guest) messages as read. `messaging:read`
(non-sensitive → **HTTP Basic** permitted). Naturally **idempotent** — a replay
is a no-op. Returns the conversation.

x-codeSamples.source:

  -u "$SH_KEY_ID:$SH_SECRET" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

get.description:
Messages within a thread. `messaging:read`. **Bodies gate on `message_content:read`**
(not contact scopes) — without it, `content` returns `"***"`.

attributes.content: Yes, it's available for those dates!

post.description:
Sends a partner-originated message into the
conversation's channel (attributed to the account's partner system user). Requires
`messaging:send` (sensitive → **HMAC**) and a **mandatory** `Idempotency-Key` — a retried
send is a duplicate guest WhatsApp/email, which is irreversible.

**Sending a photo?** Send it as its own request, with `attachment_ids` and **no**
`content`. Text and an attachment in the same request delivers the text and drops
the photo — see `SendMessageRequest`.

**`meta.delivery` says whether the guest will ever see the message. Read it.**
`201` means we accepted and stored the message, not that the channel delivered it.

  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$BODY"

post.description:
Uploads a file to Channex and returns an attachment id to pass to
`POST /conversations/{conversation_id}/messages` as `attachment_ids[]`.
**Outbound attachments are OTA-thread-only.**

The file is sent **base64 in the JSON body (not multipart)** so the request is
signable via the standard HMAC raw-body flow. Requires `messaging:send`
(sensitive → **HMAC** + `X-SH-Nonce`). Max **25 MB**; the MIME type is sniffed
from the bytes (client-declared type ignored) against an allow-list:
`image/jpeg,png,gif,webp`, `application/pdf`, `video/mp4`.

The returned id is bound to your account for 24h; the send endpoint rejects
an id minted by another account (`422 attachment_not_found`).

201.description: File uploaded; returns the Channex attachment id.

x-codeSamples.source:
TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/attachments"
BODY=$(printf '{"file":"%s","filename":"id-front.png"}' "$(base64 -i id-front.png)")
HASH=$(printf %s "$BODY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' POST "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
curl -X POST "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$BODY"

get.description:
Attachment metadata for a message. Scope `message_content:read`; account-scoped
via the conversation. Each `url` is the download endpoint below.

**302 redirect** to a short-lived signed source URL (Channex today; a re-hosted
store later — the partner contract is this endpoint). Scope `message_content:read`;
account-scoped via the conversation; every call is audit-logged. The redirect
target needs no auth, so the caller's HTTP client follows it transparently.

302.description: Redirect to the signed download URL (`Location` header).

get.description:
Lists the webhook endpoints owned by **this API key** (never the account's
host-created endpoints or another key's), newest first, keyset-paginated.
Requires `webhooks:manage` (sensitive → **HMAC**). `webhooks:manage` is a write
scope, so `X-SH-Nonce` is required here too, even though this is a GET.

TS=$(date +%s)
PATH_="/api/v1/partner/webhook_endpoints"
HASH=$(printf %s "" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d" " -f1)
CANON=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n%s' GET "$PATH_" "$TS" "$HASH")
SIG=$(printf %s "$CANON" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SH_SIGNING_SECRET" -hex | sed 's/.* //')
# webhooks:manage is a write scope → X-SH-Nonce is required even on GET.
curl "https://platform-dev.symplehost.ai$PATH_" \
  -H "X-SH-Key-Id: $SH_KEY_ID" \
  -H "X-SH-Timestamp: $TS" \
  -H "X-SH-Nonce: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.symplehost.partner.v1+json"

post.description:
Registers a webhook endpoint for **this key**. Requires `webhooks:manage`
(sensitive → **HMAC**) and an `Idempotency-Key`. The response reveals the
endpoint's `signing_secret` **exactly once**, under `meta.signing_secret` — it
is never returned again and is never serialized in the resource `attributes`,
so store it now. Use it to verify the `X-SH-Signature` on delivered events.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint that will receive event deliveries.

subscribed_events.description: Event types to subscribe to (max 32 items; each ≤ 64 chars).

payload_version.description: Optional payload version; defaults to the current version.

201.description:
Endpoint created. `meta.signing_secret` is revealed **once here only** —
persist it immediately; it is never shown again.

signing_secret.description: One-time HMAC signing secret for this endpoint. Shown only on create — store it now.

  -H "X-SH-Signature: $SIG" \

delete.description: Permanently removes one of **this key's** webhook endpoints. Requires `webhooks:manage` (sensitive → **HMAC**).

post.description:
Re-enables an endpoint that was auto-disabled after repeated delivery failures
(resets it to active). Requires `webhooks:manage` (sensitive → **HMAC**) and an
`Idempotency-Key`. The `signing_secret` is **not** re-revealed.

get.description:
Lists delivery attempts for one of **this key's** webhook endpoints, newest
first, keyset-paginated. Requires `webhooks:manage` (sensitive → **HMAC**,
and `X-SH-Nonce` even though this is a GET).

post.description:
Re-queues a past delivery for re-send. Only `dead`, `delivered`, or `failed`
deliveries may be replayed — anything else returns `409`. Requires
`webhooks:manage` (sensitive → **HMAC**) and an `Idempotency-Key`.

basicAuth.description: `Authorization: Basic base64(key_id:secret)` — read-only, non-sensitive scopes only.

hmacAuth.name: X-SH-Signature
hmacAuth.description:
HMAC-SHA256 over `"<METHOD>\n<fullpath>\n<unix_ts>\n<sha256_hex(body)>"` using the key's
`signing_secret`, hex-encoded (lowercase). `<fullpath>` includes the query string. Also send
`X-SH-Key-Id`, `X-SH-Timestamp`, and `X-SH-Nonce` (writes and all `webhooks:manage` calls;
safe to send always). 120s window. **"Try it" cannot auto-sign — use the code samples.**

UpdatedSince.name: updated_since
UpdatedSince.description: ISO-8601 seed for the first page only; afterwards use `cursor`. On endpoints that accept `sort`, seeding `updated_since` without an explicit `sort` selects the `updated_at`-ascending polling feed, overriding the default order.

Sort.name: sort
Sort.description: Sort order (default `-created_at`, newest first). A `-` prefix means descending. Supplying `updated_since` without `sort` keeps the `updated_at`-ascending polling feed. Keep the same `sort` across a paginated run — a `cursor` is only valid within the sort that minted it.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated UUID; replays return the original result.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window (IETF RateLimit).

listing_id.description: Primary listing this reservation is for (derived from the first booking's line item).

guest.description: PII per-field gated; withheld fields return "***".

phone.description: E.164. Null when no calling code is on file for this guest.

description.description: Primary listing description, sanitized to partner-safe plain text (HTML tags/entities and emoji stripped, whitespace and line-endings normalized) for PMS/OTA compatibility.

descriptions.description: Structured description sections imported from the OTA (e.g. Airbnb) and persisted on the listing, each sanitized to partner-safe plain text (HTML/entities and emoji stripped). Blank sections are omitted; an empty object `{}` when nothing was imported. The OTA `description` section is intentionally omitted here — it duplicates the top-level `description` attribute (a redundant full-text dump); `notes` carries the host's written house rules verbatim (also surfaced as `house_rules`).

interaction.description: Host interaction / availability during the stay.

example.space: Two-bedroom apartment with a private balcony and river views.
example.access: Self check-in via smart lock; code sent 24h before arrival.
example.notes: No parties. Quiet hours after 10pm. No smoking indoors.

minimum_stay.description: Effective minimum nights (listing override → account default → 1).

maximum_stay.description: Effective maximum nights (listing override → account default → 365).

cancellation_policy_type.description: Cancellation policy category (honors parent-unit inheritance). Retained for back-compat; see `cancellation_policy` for the full object.

cancellation_policy.description: Full cancellation policy (honors parent-unit inheritance): human-readable name/description plus the refund schedule and grace period. Null when no policy is set on the listing.

description.description: Free-text policy description (sanitized to plain text).
description.example: Full refund 5 days prior to arrival.

refund_rules.description: Refund schedule — percentage refunded at each hours-before-check-in tier.

additional_rules.description: Structured house rules (array). See also `house_rules` (the OTA `notes` free-text) and `guest_policy`.

house_rules.description: Host's written house rules as free text (the OTA `notes` section, same text as `descriptions.notes`), sanitized to plain text. Null when none were imported.

guest_policy.description: Consolidated guest policy — house-level permissions and stay/timing rules bundled for convenience. Each field is also exposed at the top level; this is a grouped view, not new data.

images.description: Active images ordered by display_order. `url` is the public URL (falls back to the storage copy). Images are NOT inherited from a parent unit — a unit returns only its own photos. Image metadata, including room/space category when known, is included under the existing `properties:read` scope; no separate image scope is required.

caption.description: Optional caption stored with the image.

alt_text.description: Optional accessibility/SEO text for the image.

room_category.description: Room or space category for the image when known, such as `bedroom`, `living_room`, `bathroom`, `kitchen`, or an imported channel category.

source_room_id.description: Source/channel room identifier when the image was imported with room metadata.

primary_image_url.description: Convenience hero image URL (own photos only).

currency.description: Listing's own currency first (OTA-imported listings keep their source currency), then account currency, then USD.

base_rate_season.description: The listing's base-rate pricing season (same shape as `GET /api/v1/partner/properties/{id}/pricing_settings`). Requires the `pricing:read` scope — `null` if the key lacks that scope or the listing has no base-rate season. Own season only (not inherited from a parent unit).

price.description: Base nightly rate (min == max in the system).

ota_platforms.description: Distinct OTA platform slugs (`airbnb`, `booking`, `vrbo`, `expedia`, …) the property is actively connected to via the channel manager. A platform can appear here with no entry in `ota_listing_mappings` if its external id hasn't been resolved yet. Empty for direct-only properties.

ota_listing_mappings.description: The property's identifiers on external OTAs — one entry per active channel mapping. `external_id` is the property's id on the OTA (the id visible in the OTA's own dashboard/URLs). Inactive (disconnected) mappings and mappings with no resolvable id are omitted; parents union child-unit mappings and identical `{platform, external_id}` pairs are deduped. Empty for direct-only properties.

external_ref.description: Your reference for this listing, if linked by this key.

listing_id.description: Property this enquiry is about, as a flat id for targeting availability/pricing writes. Null until the thread is linked to a property. Added in payload version 2026-08-10.

property.description: The same property, expanded. Resolved from the conversation's discussed listing, else its reservation's first booking, else the OTA-mapped listing for a pre-reservation inquiry — so it matches what the SympleHost dashboard shows for the thread. Null when the enquiry is not linked to a property yet (common on older OTA threads). `name`, `unit_number` and `listing_type` are property catalogue data and require `properties:read`; without that scope only `id` is returned and the omitted keys are listed in `masked_fields`. Added in payload version 2026-08-10.

masked_fields.description: Field paths withheld from this response because the key lacks the scope that gates them. Empty when nothing was withheld.

last_host_reply.description: The host who most recently replied in the thread. `name`/`role` reflect the real OTA replier captured from Channex (e.g. a cohost); `role` is null for in-app SympleHost replies. Null when no host has replied yet.

role.description: OTA role (e.g. HOST/COHOST); null for in-app replies.

Inquiry.description:
The dates and guest breakdown the guest **enquired about**, sourced from the OTA's enquiry event (Airbnb via Channex) and frozen at enquiry time. Added in payload version 2026-09-22.

This is NOT the booking. These values do not follow a later reservation — if the guest books different dates, `inquiry` still reports what they originally asked for. The authoritative stay dates are `start_date`/`end_date` on `GET /partner/reservations`.

Served on the conversation resource only — the message payload and the `message.created` webhook do not carry it. Fetch the conversation when you need an enquiry's dates.

Served under `messaging:read` with no additional scope, and never listed in `masked_fields`.

`null` is ambiguous by omission: it means either the thread carries no enquiry data, or the enquiry event never reached us (it is skipped when it arrives before the thread's first message creates the conversation, and there is no backfill). Expect it on older OTA threads. Treat it as "unknown", never as "no dates requested".

Each field is independently nullable, and `0` is not `null`: `"kids": 0` means the guest declared no children, `"kids": null` means the OTA did not send that field. Do not coalesce the two.

check_in.description: First night the guest enquired about.

check_out.description: Departure date the guest enquired about.

guest_count.description: Computed as `adults + kids + infants` — the same derivation `POST /partner/reservations` applies to those three fields, so a read → write round-trip does not shift the total. NOTE: Airbnb excludes infants from the guest count it shows the host, so for an enquiry with infants this reads higher than the host's Airbnb screen; the split fields below reconcile the two. `pets` is never counted as a guest.

kids.description: Children, excluding infants. Same field name reservation create accepts.

host.description: Host-side identity of the replier, set on every host-sent message (`sender_type: "User"`); null on guest/AI/system messages. Same shape as the conversation's `last_host_reply`. `name`/`role` prefer the real OTA replier captured from the channel (e.g. a cohost); for in-app replies `name` is the SympleHost user and `role` is null. Host identity — never scope-gated.

role.description: OTA role (e.g. HOST/COHOST); null for in-app replies.

conversation_id.description: The conversation thread this message belongs to (bare ID, never gated).

customer_id.description: The conversation's customer/guest this message is from (bare ID, never gated).

guest.description: Guest contact for the conversation's customer. PII per-field gated — `name` on `guest_name:read`, `email`/`phone` on `guest_contact:read`; withheld fields return "***" and are listed in `masked_fields` as `guest.name` / `guest.email` / `guest.phone`.

phone.description: E.164. Null when no calling code is on file for this guest.

attachments.description: OTA/Channex attachments. Gated on `message_content:read` — returns `[]` (and `attachments` is listed in `masked_fields`) without it. Each `url` is the SH-owned, auth-gated download endpoint (`GET .../messages/{message_id}/attachments/{id}`), NOT a raw Channex link — it 302-redirects to a short-lived signed source.

masked_fields.description: Fields withheld for lack of scope. May include `content` and `attachments` (message_content:read), `guest.name` (guest_name:read), and `guest.email` / `guest.phone` (guest_contact:read).

Attachment.description: A normalized message attachment. `url` is the SH-owned download endpoint — GET it (scope `message_content:read`) to receive a 302 redirect to a short-lived signed source.

url.description: SH download endpoint (GET → 302 to the signed source).

size.description: Bytes when known; 0 for path-only OTA attachments.

WebhookEndpoint.description: A webhook endpoint owned by the API key. Note: `signing_secret` is NEVER included in `attributes` — it is revealed exactly once via `meta.signing_secret` on create (`POST /api/v1/partner/webhook_endpoints`).

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive failed deliveries; the endpoint is auto-disabled past a threshold.

CreateReservationRequest.description:
When `listing_id` is supplied, the push creates a property booking under the
reservation, so the listing and guest count resolve everywhere in SympleHost
(reservation list, detail, calendar, availability). Your `total_amount` and
`currency` are preserved as-is — SympleHost does **not** re-price from listing
rates for partner pushes.

listing_id.description: SH listing to book (resolve via /properties or your linked external_ref). Required to link the reservation to a property.

adults.description: Number of adult guests. Recommended. Drives the reservation's guest count.

infants.description: Number of infants. Defaults to 0. Counts toward the guest total.

guest_count.description: Legacy total guest count. Still accepted and mapped to `adults` when `adults` is omitted. Prefer the explicit `adults` / `kids` fields.

status.description: Reservation status on creation. Defaults to `confirmed` (a pushed direct booking is already booked). Send `pending` to create it awaiting confirmation instead.

currency.description: The booking's currency, recorded as provided (your own/partner currency).

total_amount.description: Your authoritative booking total. Preserved as-is (no re-pricing).

payment_status.description: Whether the booking is already paid. Defaults to `pending` (amount due = total). Send `paid` to mark it fully settled. For partial payments, send `amount_paid` instead.

amount_paid.description: Amount already collected by the partner. Overrides `payment_status`: ≥ total → paid, > 0 → partially_paid, else pending. `amount_due` is derived as total − amount_paid.

special_requests.description: Free-text guest requests, stored on the booking.

notes.description: Internal note stored on the reservation.

external_ref.description: Your booking reference (for idempotent dedupe + linking).

email.description: Optional. When omitted on a listing-backed push, a deterministic `@guest.symplehost.ai` address is generated (from the phone when present) so the property booking has a guest email.

SendMessageRequest.description:
`content` is required unless at least one `attachment_ids` entry is present (an attachment-only send).

**Do not send `content` and `attachment_ids` in the same request.** The upstream OTA messaging API accepts *either* text *or* one attachment per message, and **silently ignores the attachment when text is present** — the guest receives the text only, and the stored message comes back with an empty `attachments` array. Send the text as one request and each photo as its own attachment-only request.

content.description: Message body. Optional when `attachment_ids` has at least one entry — and on an attachment send you must omit it entirely, or the attachment is silently dropped. See the schema description above.

attachment_ids.description:
Channex attachment ids from `POST /api/v1/partner/attachments`. OTA threads only — a non-OTA conversation returns `422 attachments_unsupported`. Each id must have been uploaded by **your account** (valid 24h) — an id you did not upload returns `422 attachment_not_found`.

One attachment is delivered per underlying OTA message: several ids here fan out to one message each, in the order given. Pair them with a **blank** `content` — see the schema description above.

channel.description: Optional; defaults to the conversation's channel.

RespondToReviewRequest.description: The host reply text, JSON:API-shaped. A top-level `response` is also accepted.

response.description: The host response to post to the review.
response.example: Thank you so much for the kind words — we'd love to host you again!

file.description: Base64-encoded file bytes (≤ 25 MB decoded; base64 inflates this to ~33 MB on the wire, so size your HTTP timeouts against the encoded length). Sent in the JSON body (not multipart) so the request is HMAC-signable.

block_reason.description: Defaults to the generic "blocked" when omitted. Pass "owner_block" only for a deliberate owner hold — it feeds owner-attributable reporting. (Default changed from "owner_block" in 2026-07.)

price.description: Base nightly rate (min == max in the system).

base_guest_count.description: Guests included before the extra-guest fee.

UpdatePricingSettingsRequest.description: Partial update — send only the fields to change. Discounts are 0–100; prices > 0.

price.description: Base nightly rate; sets both bounds. (min_price/max_price still accepted for backward compatibility.)

stay_review_id.description: Id of the same review on the host-facing portal, where reviews are addressed as stay reviews rather than channel reviews. Use it to correlate a reply posted here with what the host sees. null when the review never matched a booking.

rating.description: 1–10 scale (nullable for rating-only or textless reviews).

review_text.example: A lovely stay, spotless and well located.

status.description: Lifecycle of the review on the channel. `published` is live on the OTA and readable by anyone; `hidden` is held back by the OTA (double-blind period or a takedown); `pending` means no channel state has been recorded yet — before 2026-09-21 every ingested review sat there, so treat `pending` on an older review as "unknown", not as "awaiting publication". The remaining values are moderation decisions made in SympleHost for the direct-booking site and are never written by channel sync.

reviewed_at.description: When the guest posted the review on the OTA.

can_reply.description: Whether a first reply should be submitted to the OTA. Airbnb stays true until a host response exists (Channex expired_at is informational). Other OTAs honour reply_deadline. POST .../respond submits to the OTA when true.

reply_deadline.description: Channex expired_at when present. Informational for Airbnb; enforced for other OTAs.

reply_status.description: Delivery outcome of `host_response`. `published` reached the OTA and the guest can see it. `not_deliverable` was recorded locally only because the OTA reply window is shut. `failed` was rejected by the OTA, in which case `host_response` is absent. `pending` was submitted but the outcome was never recorded. `null` means no OTA delivery was ever attempted (a direct review, or a reply stored before this field existed).

reply_error.description: Why the reply was not published, when reply_status is failed or not_deliverable.

ota_is_replied.description: The OTA's own flag: `true` means the channel shows a host reply, whose text may never have been synced here. `null` means no payload has said either way. Together with `reply_status: published` it is what makes a further POST .../respond a `409`.

category_scores.description: Per-category ratings (1–10) keyed by category, e.g. clean, communication, checkin, accuracy, location, value. Keys vary by OTA; empty object when no breakdown was provided.

attributes.description: PII per-field gated; withheld fields return "***".

phone.description: E.164 (e.g. "+15551234567"). Gated on guest_contact:read. Null when the account has no calling code on file for this customer.

count.description: Number of items in this page (always emitted).

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error code — branch on this.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation; safe to surface to operators.

errors.title: Auth invalid key
errors.detail: Provide HTTP Basic (key_id:secret) or HMAC headers.

errors.title: Signature expired
errors.detail: Timestamp missing or outside the 120s window.

NotFound.description: Not found (or not in your account).

Conflict.description: Request conflicts with the resource's current state — e.g. replaying a webhook delivery that is not in a replayable state (only `dead` / `delivered` / `failed` deliveries may be replayed).

errors.title: Idempotency key required
errors.detail: Idempotency-Key header is required for this write.
